topArticle.title: Trump administration diverts human rights funds to push far-right agenda
topArticle.description:
Support for white Afrikaners, anti-communism and others reveals how US redefining what qualifies as human rights
With hours left before the funding expires, the Trump administration is pushing to direct more than $175m of the state department’s flagship human rights fund to a slate of awards that includes a huge $40m grant for an anti-communism fund, support for a group advancing white Afrikaner rights in South Africa, a campaign against Brazil’s supreme court, and programs that would reward ideological allies in Europe who protect “western civilizational norms”.
On Wednesday, the state department obligated the funds to the grantees hours before the deadline despite congressional concerns and requests to not do so, according to a source familiar with the negotiations. The Guardian has reached out to the state department for comment on whether it had “blown” holds from Congress on releasing the funds due to concerns about their use.
 Continue reading...

topArticle.title: At least 27 dead after two mass shootings in South Africa, police say
topArticle.description:
Seventeen people killed near Johannesburg in suspected ‘illegal goldmining turf war’, as 10 killed in separate incident at barbecue venue near Cape Town
Two separate mass shootings near South Africa’s two biggest cities killed at least 27 people, as the country grapples with one of the world’s highest murder rates amid investigations into corruption and criminality within the police.
The South African police service said on Sunday that 17 people were killed on Saturday night when eight suspects armed with AK-47 assault rifles and pistols opened fire at a bar in Wedela township, about 50 miles south-west of central Johannesburg. At least 15 other people sustained gunshot injuries in that attack, police said.

topArticle.title: Burundi agrees to receive ‘third-country’ migrant deportees from US
topArticle.description:
Burundi joins several other African nations in accepting people deported under Trump’s hardline policy
Burundi has agreed to join a clutch of ⁠other African nations in receiving migrants from other countries deported from the US under ⁠Donald Trump’s hardline ⁠immigration ​policy.
However, the authorities in Bujumbura, the country’s economic capital, said Burundi will only accept those not accused of crime or terrorism links, said ⁠Nancy Ninette Mutoni, a spokesperson for the country’s president, Évariste Ndayishimiye. Tuesday’s announcement gave no details of numbers, timing or financial ⁠details.
 Continue reading...

topArticle.title: DRC politician beaten to death after radio appearance about Ebola outbreak
topArticle.description:
Marie-Celestin Karondwa was attacked on Sunday after promoting measures to prevent spread of disease, his party says

A senior member of the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s ruling party was beaten to death on Sunday after appearing on a radio programme to raise awareness about the Ebola outbreak, a party representative has said.
Marie-Celestin Karondwa, the acting president of the Union for Democracy and Social Progress (UDPS) party’s federal executive committee in Butembo, a new hotspot for the outbreak, was attacked after taking part in a ​radio show during which he ‌promoted prevention measures for the disease, ‌the UDPS federation in the city said in a statement, Reuters reported.
 Continue reading...

topArticle.title: Melbourne man’s mysterious disappearance on popular Peru hiking trail prompts widespread search
topArticle.description:
Loved ones describe Jordan Yap, 30, as an experienced hiker who set out for a 10-day solo trek Peru before falling silent

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Loved ones of a missing Australian trekker who was last seen nearly two weeks ago on a remote South American hiking trail are urging local authorities to help with the search.
A wide-scale sweep by a private rescue crew has so far failed to find any trace of 30-year-old Jordan Yap, who last made contact with friends and family on 14 September ahead of a planned 10-day solo trek along Peru’s Huayhuash mountain range, 400km north-east of Lima.

topArticle.description: The suspect, 24, was arrested before the alleged cyber attack took place.
topArticle.titleJa: オランダ警察、FBIハックを主張するグループの容疑者を逮捕
topArticle.summary: オランダ警察は、FBIへのサイバー攻撃を主張するグループの一員とされる24歳の容疑者を逮捕しました。容疑者は攻撃発生前に拘束されました。

topArticle.title: Estonia blames Russia for arson at defence company supplying Ukraine
topArticle.description: Russia has been accused of launching sabotage attacks across a number of European Nato countries which have been helping Ukraine.
topArticle.titleJa: エストニア、ウクライナ供給の防衛企業放火をロシアのせいに
topArticle.summary: エストニアは、ウクライナに物資を供給する防衛企業での放火事件についてロシアを非難しました。ロシアはNATO加盟国への妨害行為を数多く仕掛けているとされています。

topArticle.title: Rights group accuses Vietnam of abducting Australian and Norwegian activists
topArticle.description: Vietnam says the men entered the country illegally and accused them of planning terrorist activities.
topArticle.titleJa: 人権団体、ベトナムが豪州とノルウェーの活動家を誘拐したと非難
topArticle.summary: 人権団体は、ベトナムがオーストラリアとノルウェーの活動家を誘拐したと非難しています。ベトナム側は、彼らが不法入国しテロ活動を計画していたと主張しています。

topArticle.title: Czech Republic ready for Wembley 30 years after Euro '96
topArticle.description: The Czech Republic are returning to Wembley for a Nations League game with England, just over 30 years after their Euro '96 heartbreak there.
topArticle.titleJa: チェコ共和国、ユーロ'96から30年ぶりにウェンブリーへ
topArticle.summary: チェコ共和国が、ユーロ'96での苦い思い出から30年以上ぶりにウェンブリーに戻り、イングランドとのネーションズリーグ戦に臨みます。

topArticle.title: Hurricane Polo makes landfall on Mexico's Pacific coast
topArticle.description: The storm moved ashore on the Baja California peninsula, which is a popular tourist destination.
topArticle.titleJa: ハリケーン・ポロ、メキシコ太平洋岸に上陸
topArticle.summary: ハリケーン・ポロがメキシコのバハ・カリフォルニア半島に上陸。人気観光地が影響を受ける。

topArticle.title: Argentina threatens legal action against UK over Falkland Islands oil exploration
topArticle.description: President Javier Milei set a two-week deadline for the Sea Lion oilfield project to be scrapped.
topArticle.titleJa: アルゼンチン、フォークランド諸島での石油探査を巡り英国を法的措置で脅す
topArticle.summary: アルゼンチンのミレイ大統領が、フォークランド諸島沖での石油探査中止を英国に要求し、法的措置を示唆した。

topArticle.title: Venezuela’s earthquakes leave children facing trauma, displacement and food insecurity
topArticle.description: As families seek refuge, Venezuela’s youngest children grapple with fear, disrupted routines and the loss of basic nutritional security.
topArticle.titleJa: ベネズエラの地震、子供たちにトラウマ、避難、食料不安をもたらす
topArticle.summary: ベネズエラでの地震により、幼い子供たちは恐怖、日常生活の混乱、基本的な栄養保障の喪失といった深刻な問題に直面しており、家族は避難を余儀なくされています。

topArticle.title: New wild cat species discovered - with only one known living member
topArticle.description: A spotted wildcat long mistaken for relatives has been identified as a new species in Bolivia.
topArticle.titleJa: 新種の野生ネコ発見 - 既知の現存個体は1匹のみ
topArticle.summary: ボリビアで、これまで近縁種と誤認されていた新種の野生ネコが発見されたが、既知の個体はわずか1匹である。

topArticle.title: ‘Pay-by-the-day’ living in Pereira: The forgotten survivors of Colombia’s earthquake
topArticle.description: In Pereira, Colombia, earthquake survivors living in pay-by-the-day rooms now face homelessness, overcrowded shelters, illness, and a struggle to be counted.
topArticle.titleJa: ペレイラでの「日払い」生活：コロンビア地震の忘れられた生存者たち
topArticle.summary: コロンビアのペレイラでは、地震の生存者たちが日払い部屋に住み、ホームレス化、過密な避難所、病気、そして存在を認識されない苦境に直面しています。

topArticle.title: New Zealand advances safe and inclusive trade with new contribution to STDF
topArticle.description: New Zealand has contributed NZ$ 300,000 (approximately CHF 140,000) to the Standards and Trade Development Facility (STDF) to help developing and least-developed countries, including in the Pacific, strengthen food safety and animal and plant health systems.
topArticle.titleJa: ニュージーランド、STDFへの新たな貢献で安全かつ包括的な貿易を推進
topArticle.summary: ニュージーランドはSTDFに30万NZドルを拠出し、発展途上国、特に太平洋地域の食品安全と動植物の健康システム強化を支援する。

topArticle.title: Watch: Luxury prison in Indonesia demolished after public outcry
topArticle.description: Indonesian lawmakers on Wednesday ordered the demolition of a controversial luxury compound inside a penitentiary near the capital.
topArticle.titleJa: インドネシアの豪華刑務所、世論の反発を受け解体へ
topArticle.summary: インドネシアの首都近郊にある刑務所内の物議を醸した豪華施設が、国民の強い反発を受け解体命令が出された。

topArticle.title: Watch: Bangkok locals create floating market during floods
topArticle.description: As sellers waded through floodwaters to sell produce like fish and vegetables from floating platforms and foam boxes, buyers walked or paddled between the makeshift stalls to buy their groceries.
topArticle.titleJa: バンコクの地元住民、洪水時に水上マーケットを開設
topArticle.summary: 洪水に見舞われたバンコクで、地元の住民が生活物資を売買するため、水上マーケットを開設し、困難な状況下での適応力を見せた。

topArticle.title: Malaysia begins controversial repatriation of asylum seekers to Myanmar
topArticle.description: Human rights groups say some 5,000 returnees could face violence, persecution and forced conscription.
topArticle.titleJa: マレーシア、ミャンマーへの難民送還を開始し物議
topArticle.summary: マレーシアが難民約5,000人をミャンマーへ送還する計画を開始。人権団体は暴力や迫害のリスクを懸念し、物議を醸している。

topArticle.title: Four bodies found after avalanche hits Himalayan climbing group
topArticle.description: Rescuers are still looking for 12 Nepalese cook staff who were preparing for climbers to ascend the Himlung Himal peak.
topArticle.titleJa: ヒマラヤ登山隊を雪崩が襲い、4遺体を発見
topArticle.summary: ヒマラヤ登山隊を雪崩が襲い、4人の遺体が見つかった。さらに12人のネパール人調理スタッフが行方不明のまま。
